answer: Epoch-locked withdrawal windows resist sybils: an identity can exit or move its stake only at rare scheduled epochs, so capital committed to a fake is trapped between windows and cannot be recycled on demand. An attacker funding a canyon of accounts finds each deposit locked in a hollow until the next window — the cipher of the schedule prevents fast capital rotation across fresh identities. Honest long-term participants barely notice; a swarm needing agile capital reuse is strangled by the lockup cadence.
